newsitem.title: CANADA: Potash Arcadian deal to lift EPS 25 pct - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Potash Arcadian deal to lift EPS 25 pct - CEO.

text.p: Potash Corp of Saskatchewan expects its US$1.18-billion acquisition of Arcadian Corp to mean a big boost to both earnings and cash flow per share, Potash chairman, president and chief executive Chuck Childers said on Tuesday.
"It's a very, very accretive acquisition for the PCS shareholders," Childers said in an interview.
Childers said the company combined the forecasts of seven prominent North American fertilizer analysts that cover both firms in evaluating in the deal.

Based on the analyst models of the two firms and including goodwill, interest payments for the cash portion and some synergies, net income per share would be accretive by 22 to 25 percent, he said. Cash flow per share was expected to be accretive by 30 percent.

The Potash bid, which eclipsed a proposed merger between Arcadian and Freeport-McMoRan Inc, was aimed at adding nitrogen to Potash's product slate, a move that would see it becoming a top global producer of that as well as potash and phosphate.
Saskatoon-based Potash fell C$3.25 to C$100.25 in Toronto and by $2.38 to $73.63 on the New York Stock Exchange on Tuesday.
Apart from the cash and stock portion of the deal, valued at between UD$25 and US$27 per share, Potash would also assume US$525 million in debt and about US$300 million in cash.
Childers said Arcadian's size and low share price made for an attractive acquisition target.

"They are the largest (nitrogen producer) in the Western Hemisphere," he said. "It's been our strategy and our operating procedure to try and be as big a force as we can in any of the commodities we get into."
He said that, because Arcadian's shares were trading so low compared with its asset value it made it the most likely nitrogen producer target.
Also, Arcadian has several industrial customers that buy nitrogen products for stable prices, a desirable factor in the volatile market, he said.
Childers said also he anticipated that the company's talks to acquire BASF AG's 51 percent stake in German potash company Kali und Salz AG would also result in a deal.
"That's a blockbuster acquisition as well," he said.
